answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using time-locked collateral bonds per public key. Before an agent can wander into active markets, it escrows tokens in a contract that slashes deposits on signed equivocation or default proofs, preventing a plume of disposable keys. Attackers thus incur the verifiable cost of illiquid capital per identity, perched on a financial ledge where misconduct loses funds. However, wealthy adversaries can still fund large clusters of compliant accounts.
